output.summary: A perennial wetland herb native across most of Eurasia and locally in northwestern Africa, narrow-leaved cattail grows in fresh or brackish water. Its slender leaves overtop the flowering stem, whose upper male and lower female sections are separated by a conspicuous bare gap; the female section matures into a rusty-brown, sausage-shaped spike.
output.edibilityNote: Depending on season, edible parts include dormant root and leaf-base sprouts, stalk cores, green flower spikes, ripe pollen and starchy roots; prepare like broadleaf cattail.
